options.content: **How to read it.** The top row is now. Below, every timeline is one row per Pod or per reason, coloured over time; select a range on any graph with the mouse to replay what happened in it (a switchover, a failover, a rolling update), and read it to the millisecond in *What happened*. Vertical markers on every graph come from the log of the operator: **blue** a switchover, **red** a failover, **purple** a rolling update, **orange** another Event; the switches at the top name them, hover a marker for its text.

panels.title: Primary
panels.description: The Pod in status.currentPrimary: the one -rw sends clients to

panels.title: Primary epoch
panels.description: Grows by one with every switchover and failover

panels.title: Ready instances
panels.description: Ready Pods of status.readyInstances, and spec.instances

panels.title: Ready
panels.description: The condition Ready: green with reason Ready, red with the reason why not

panels.title: Alerts
panels.description: The alerts of config/monitoring/prometheusrule.yaml that fire now or fired in the range; hover a bar for the labels. Nothing here: none fired.

targets.expr: max by (alertname) (ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",name="$instance"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",persistentvolumeclaim=~"$instance-[0-9]+-data"}) or (max by (alertname) (max_over_time((ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",name="$instance"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"} or ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="$namespace",persistentvolumeclaim=~"$instance-[0-9]+-data"})[$__range:15s])) * 0 - 1)

panels.title: Operations: everything the operator (and the Instance Managers) did to it
Switchovers
panels.description: Completed planned moves of the primary of this instance

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$instance","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind | drop fields |= `"kind": "switchover"` !~ `"outcome": "(rejected|failed|interrupted)"` [$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Failovers
panels.description: Failovers of this instance

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$instance","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind | drop fields |= `"kind": "failover"` [$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Rejected or failed
panels.description: Switchovers and recreates the operator rejected (e.g. a target that is not Ready, the primary), that failed (the target did not catch up in a minute) or that a failover interrupted

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$instance","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind | drop fields |~ `"outcome": "(rejected|failed|interrupted)"` [$__range])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Slowest switchover
panels.description: From the start of the switchover until the target is the primary

targets.expr: max(max_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$instance","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind, durationMs | drop fields |= `"kind": "switchover"` !~ `"outcome": "(rejected|failed|interrupted)"` | unwrap durationMs [$__range]))

panels.title: Slowest failover
panels.description: From the start of the failover until the target is the primary

targets.expr: max(max_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$instance","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind, durationMs | drop fields |= `"kind": "failover"` !~ `"outcome": "(rejected|failed|interrupted)"` | unwrap durationMs [$__range]))

panels.title: Longest primary outage
panels.description: How long a primary was unavailable before a failover or a safe start ended

targets.expr: max(max_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$instance","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind, downMs | drop fields | unwrap downMs [$__range]))

panels.title: Every operation (click one for its logs)
panels.description: One row per switchover, failover, rolling update, safe start, recreate (asked for), volume replaced (a PVC of a replica deleted or lost), configuration (spec.redis applied or rejected by Redis), certificate (issued or updated), scale up or down, and self-fence (the Instance Manager paused the writes of the primary while it could not reach the API server), from the line logged when it ends, with its outcome and why it started. Took: from its start to its end; for a volume, until the replica is Ready again on the new one, after its full sync. Primary down: for a failover or a safe start, since the primary became unavailable. Click the kind of a row: the dashboard opens on the seconds of that operation, and *What happened, to the millisecond* shows every log line of it, of the operator and of the Pods.

targets.expr: {namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$instance","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind, outcome, name, from, to, epoch, durationMs, downMs, reason, startMs, endMs | label_format linkFrom=`{{ if .startMs }}{{ sub .startMs 3000 }}{{ end }}`, linkTo=`{{ if .endMs }}{{ add .endMs 5000 }}{{ end }}`, outcome=`{{ or .outcome "completed" }}`, inst=`{{ .name }}` | drop fields

panels.title: How long each one took
panels.description: A point per operation at the moment it ended; the height is how long it took (log scale)

targets.expr: max by (kind) (max_over_time({namespace=~"redis-operator-system|$namespace", container=~"manager|redis"} |~ `\{"name":"$instance","namespace":"$namespace"\}` |~ `(Completed|Finished) (switchover|failover|rolling update|safe start|recreate|volume replaced|configuration|certificate|scale up|scale down|self-fence)` | regexp `\t(?P<fields>\{.*\})$` | line_format `{{.fields}}` | json kind, durationMs | drop fields !~ `"outcome": "(rejected|failed|interrupted)"` | unwrap durationMs [$__interval]))

panels.title: What happened, to the millisecond
panels.description: The log of the operator about this instance and the logs of its Pods (Redis, the Instance Manager, the exporter), in order. Select the time of a switchover or failover on a graph to read it step by step: the fence, the promotion, REPLICAOF, the partial resync.

targets.expr: {namespace="redis-operator-system", container="manager"} |~ `\{"name":"$instance","namespace":"$namespace"\}` != `Moved slot` | regexp `^\S+\t(?P<level>\S+)\t(?:events\t)?(?P<msg>[^\t]+)` | regexp `"reason": "(?P<reason>[^"]+)"` | regexp `"error": "(?P<error>(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"` | line_format `operator  {{.msg}} {{.reason}} {{.error}}`

panels.title: Role of every Pod
panels.description: Green: the primary. Orange: the replica the operator is promoting (status.targetPrimary). The green bar jumping rows is a switchover or a failover.

panels.title: Pod Ready (kubelet)
panels.description: Red while a Pod restarts, or a replica has not finished its first sync

panels.title: Conditions: one row each, the text is the reason
panels.description: Every condition of the RedisInstance on one row; the bar shows its reason over time. Green: fine (Ready, Applied, Issued). Grey: idle (Completed). Orange: something runs (InProgress, RollingUpdate, Switchover). Red: a problem (PrimaryUnavailable, Failed, ...).

panels.title: Replication: who replicates from whom, and where it runs
panels.description: Every Pod with the machine it runs on and its commands per second (green the primary, blue a replica); every arrow a replica, with the bytes per second it replicates.

targets.expr: sum by (id, title, subtitle, color) (label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(label_replace(sum by (pod, node, role) ((rate(redis_commands_processed_total{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) and redis_commands_processed_total{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}) * on (pod) group_left (node) max by (pod, pod_ip, node) (kube_pod_info{namespace="$namespace",pod=~"$instance-[0-9]+"})), "id", "$1", "pod", "(.*)"), "title", "$1", "pod", "(.*)"), "subtitle", "$1", "node", "(.*)"), "color", "green", "role", "primary"), "color", "blue", "role", "replica"))

sum by (id, source, target) (label_join(label_replace(label_replace(sum by (pod, slave_ip) (deriv(redis_connected_slave_offset_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}[$__rate_interval]) and redis_connected_slave_offset_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}) * on (slave_ip) group_left (replica) label_replace(label_replace(max by (pod, pod_ip, node) (kube_pod_info{namespace="$namespace",pod=~"$instance-[0-9]+"}), "replica", "$1", "pod", "(.*)"), "slave_ip", "$1", "pod_ip", "(.*)"), "source", "$1", "pod", "(.*)"), "target", "$1", "replica", "(.*)"), "id", "->", "source", "target"))

panels.title: Replication throughput per replica
panels.description: Bytes per second each replica takes from its primary: the write traffic of the primary

targets.expr: sum by (pod, slave_ip) ((deriv(redis_connected_slave_offset_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) and on (pod, slave_ip) redis_connected_slave_offset_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}) * on (slave_ip) group_left (replica) label_replace(label_replace(max by (pod, pod_ip, node) (kube_pod_info{namespace="$namespace",pod=~"$instance-[0-9]+"}), "replica", "$1", "pod", "(.*)"), "slave_ip", "$1", "pod_ip", "(.*)")

panels.title: Lag of every replica
panels.description: The most bytes of writes the replica had not acknowledged in each minute, as its primary sees it. A replica acknowledges once a second, so up to a second of writes is normal; a line that keeps growing is a replica that falls behind.

targets.expr: sum by (pod, slave_ip) ((max_over_time((max by (pod) (redis_master_repl_offset{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}) - on (pod) group_right redis_connected_slave_offset_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"})[1m:])) and on (pod, slave_ip) redis_connected_slave_offset_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}) * on (slave_ip) group_left (replica) label_replace(label_replace(max by (pod, pod_ip, node) (kube_pod_info{namespace="$namespace",pod=~"$instance-[0-9]+"}), "replica", "$1", "pod", "(.*)"), "slave_ip", "$1", "pod_ip", "(.*)")

panels.title: Resyncs served in the time range
panels.description: Full: the primary sent a whole snapshot (a new or a lost replica). Partial: a replica caught up from the backlog, e.g. after a switchover.

panels.title: Commands per second
panels.description: A dip on the primary is the pause of a switchover or the gap of a failover

panels.title: Keys
panels.description: Equal on every Pod once the replicas are in sync

panels.title: Main thread busy
panels.description: Redis runs commands on one thread: at 100 % a node can do no more, however many cores the machine has. Add shards, not CPUs.

panels.title: CPU throttled by the limit
panels.description: Share of the time the kernel held Redis back for its CPU limit: latency spikes even when the average looks fine. Empty without a CPU limit.

panels.title: Commands per second, every master
panels.description: Lines far apart: a hot shard, with hot keys or more slots; Redis 7.2 has no numbers per slot

panels.title: Memory of every master, of maxmemory
panels.description: At 100 %: with noeviction writes fail with OOM (see the errors), with an allkeys-* policy keys are evicted

targets.expr: max by (namespace, pod) (redis_memory_used_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}) / max by (namespace, pod) (redis_memory_max_bytes{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}) and on (namespace, pod) (redis_operator_instance_pod_role{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"} == 1)

panels.title: Container memory, of its limit
panels.description: maxmemory plus the copy of a fork (BGSAVE, AOF rewrite, full resync), client and replica buffers: at 100 % the kernel OOMKills Redis

panels.title: Network of every node
panels.description: Clients, replication and MIGRATE; the cluster bus has its own port

panels.title: Output buffers
panels.description: A replica over the soft limit for a minute, or over the hard one, is dropped and comes back with a full resync, which under load may repeat. The hard limit (256 MB by default) may be above the memory limit of the Pod.

panels.title: Seconds of writes the backlog holds
panels.description: A replica cut off for longer than this needs a full resync instead of a partial one. Seconds under heavy writes: raise repl-backlog-size in spec.redis.parameters.

targets.expr: max by (namespace, pod) (redis_config_repl_backlog_size{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}) / (max by (namespace, pod) (deriv(redis_master_repl_offset{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}[1m])) > 0) and on (namespace, pod) (redis_operator_instance_pod_role{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"} == 1)

panels.title: Changes of the master
panels.description: Every switchover or failover; the markers say which

panels.title: Stalls
panels.description: How long Redis stopped: the last fork, and the latest spike of every kind from LATENCY LATEST (set latency-monitor-threshold, e.g. 100 ms, in spec.redis.parameters).

panels.title: Restarts in the time range
panels.description: Of the redis container; kubectl describe pod tells OOMKilled

panels.title: Errors Redis answered, by error
panels.description: What clients got back: READONLY right after a switchover, NOREPLICAS with minReplicasToWrite, WRONGPASS or NOPERM for users, MOVED and ASK while slots move, CLUSTERDOWN, BUSYKEY. Commands of the operator count too (e.g. an ERR of a refused parameter).

panels.title: Link of every replica to its master
panels.description: Red: the replica has lost its master (master_link_status:down), e.g. after the master restarted on a new IP. A replica can be Ready while its link is down.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Reads that found their key; empty while nothing reads

panels.title: Evicted and expired keys per second
panels.description: Evicted: removed to stay below maxmemory (maxmemoryPolicy); with noeviction writes fail instead. Expired: their TTL ran out

panels.title: Latency p99, by command
panels.description: Time Redis spent on a command, without the network; the commands of the operator and the exporter are left out

panels.title: Slow log entries
panels.description: Commands slower than slowlog-log-slower-than (10 ms); read them with SLOWLOG GET

panels.title: Memory fragmentation
panels.description: RSS / used memory: about 1 to 1.5 is fine; above, memory is lost to fragmentation; below 1, swapping

panels.title: Last fork took
panels.description: Redis stops while it forks for an RDB save, an AOF rewrite or a full resync; grows with the dataset

panels.title: Saving in the background
panels.description: 1 while an RDB save or an AOF rewrite runs

panels.title: Rejected connections and blocked clients
panels.description: Rejected: over maxclients. Blocked: clients waiting in BLPOP, XREAD BLOCK, WAIT

panels.title: Connected replicas of the primary
panels.description: Replicas the primary streams to; below spec.instances - 1 a replica is down or syncing

targets.expr: max by (namespace, pod) (redis_connected_slaves{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}) and on (namespace, pod) (redis_operator_instance_pod_role{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"} == 1)

panels.title: Keys by type and memory, now
panels.description: Every Pod samples 200 random keys at every scrape (RANDOMKEY, TYPE, MEMORY USAGE) and counts them by type and memory: a share of the keys, not exact. A rare type or a few big keys may not show; redis-cli --bigkeys finds those.

targets.expr: sum by (key) (avg by (redis_instance, key) (redis_script_values{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"})) / scalar(sum(avg by (redis_instance, key) (redis_script_values{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"})))

panels.title: Keys by type over time
panels.description: Share of the sampled keys by type; with Keys it tells how many of each

targets.expr: sum by (type) (label_replace(avg by (redis_instance, key) (redis_script_values{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"}), "type", "$1", "key", "(\\S+) .*")) / scalar(sum(avg by (redis_instance, key) (redis_script_values{namespace="$namespace",redis_instance="$instance"})))

panels.title: Volumes used
panels.description: Used space of every PVC, from the kubelet; orange from 70 %, red from 85 %

panels.title: AOF size
panels.description: The append-only file grows with every write and shrinks at a rewrite

panels.title: Since the last RDB save
panels.description: How old the snapshot on the volume is; with persistence aof the AOF has the writes since

panels.title: State of every volume
panels.description: status.volumes, a row per instance: Ready green; Terminating orange (the PVC is being deleted, the operator moves the replica to a new one); Missing or Lost red; Detached grey (scaled down). A state of a few seconds may fall between two scrapes: the table of operations has every volume replaced.
